clue.text: Joint problems of hairiest sort to treat

indicators.note: to treat material is to process or work on it, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that the hairiest kind of person suffers joint trouble that needs treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treat' is the anagram signal acting on HAIRIEST, SORT and TO together; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition is a wearing-down of cartilage that causes painful, stiff joints.

clue.text: No cigar is turned out without using chemicals

indicators.note: something turned out is produced afresh, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cigar that has not been produced at all, apparently made without chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is turned out' is the anagram signal for NO CIGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic farming and produce avoid synthetic fertilisers and pesticides.

clue.text: Unsound artistic production of play set in Rome

indicators.note: a production is something made or staged, so the fodder's letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a shaky, arty staging of a Roman drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' is the anagram signal acting on UNSOUND ARTISTIC; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's bloodiest tragedy is set in ancient Rome among its emperors and Goths.

clue.text: More than ancient history, some say

definitions.meaning: people say of a finished affair that it is all done with, past and gone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means 'exceeding' and also describes something finished, as when people call a relationship ancient history.

clue.text: Upcountry rugby's given endless credit

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union, with the possessive S

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the word for credit is dropped

parts.note: on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: A country rugby club has been allowed to run up a tab.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK (British slang for credit, as in 'buying on tick') loses its last letter under 'endless' to give TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe rural places and people away from the town.

clue.text: Hail tuba arrangement as standard

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks a piece, here the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A brass-band setting of a welcome piece for tuba becomes the usual fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' is the anagram signal for HAIL TUBA; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean usual or customary, what is done as a matter of course.

clue.text: Multiply without going forth?

parts.note: plays on the biblical 'go forth and multiply': breeding that stays within a group rather than going outside it

explanation.surface: A twist on the biblical command to be fruitful and spread across the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeding among members of a closed population is reproduction that stays inside the group.

clue.text: Private house?

parts.note: house is the theatre word for the people watching, and private means admission by request only

explanation.surface: Reads as a question about a dwelling that is not public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like a home but is the theatre sense, the people in the seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's house is its spectators, and one admitted only by invitation is a private one.

clue.text: Artist with one fault-the grape, that was!

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
the Roman numeral I is one
a sin is a moral fault

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a painter's failing has withered like a grape.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried fruit that began life fresh on the vine, hence a grape in its former state.

clue.text: Good states of channels

parts.note: to state something is to say it aloud, to utter it

explanation.surface: A heading about the proper condition of waterways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' looks like a noun (conditions) but is the verb, says; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are grooves or troughs carrying water away, as along a roof edge or street.

clue.text: Cricketer with a way in old Holland

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket reporting
via is Latin for road or way

explanation.surface: A cricket player and a route somewhere in the Netherlands of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is often just 'a bat'; 'with' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name for the Low Countries' region, later the Batavian Republic of the Netherlands.

clue.text: Comfy home in Gladstone Street

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of letters of the street name

explanation.surface: A cosy house on a road named after the Victorian prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the letters inside GLADSTONE STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's dwelling is used figuratively for a snug family dwelling.

clue.text: Delivery statistics of Erith brats, for example?

indicators.note: the question mark hints the children are an example of what is counted, and the words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Records of babies born, illustrated by the unruly children of a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: ERITH is a town in south-east London. The anagram is signalled only loosely, by 'for example?', the brats being examples of what is counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures for the number of babies delivered per head of population.

clue.text: Normal pies cooked cold.

indicators.note: food that is cooked is changed, as are the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Ordinary pies have been baked and left to go cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold' looks like a temperature but means aloof; 'cooked' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a manner lacking warmth or personal feeling.

clue.text: Extraordinarily manic English films

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of its usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A review praising wildly frantic British movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinarily' rearranges MANIC with E for English.
explanation.definitionFit: The pictures collectively, as in going to the films or going to the pictures.

clue.text: Ugly old figure, she has tweed shortened and altered

indicators.note: cut short, so the cloth's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Harris tweed is a famous cloth from the Outer Hebrides

indicators.note: something altered is changed, so the letters of the little word are reordered

explanation.surface: A grim old woman gets her tweed suit taken up and refitted.
explanation.walkthrough: HARRIS tweed, a Scottish island cloth, is 'shortened' to HARRI; 'altered' turns AND into DAN. 'she has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad-tempered, unattractive elderly woman, a crone or battleaxe.

clue.text: … and soon divided, and the like

definitions.meaning: 'soon' split into two words makes the phrase 'and so on'

explanation.surface: An unfinished sentence trailing off into a list.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'soon' and you get 'and so on', the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'and the rest', used to stand for 'and so on' or 'and similar things'.

clue.text: Large cigar producing flawless ring

parts.note: without flaw means perfect
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A big cigar that blows a perfect smoke ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick cigar tapered at both ends, a Cuban style.

clue.text: The King and I put on in college, but in cramped style

indicators.note: a show put on in a venue is staged inside it, so these letters go inside the college

parts.note: a poly is a polytechnic, a British college
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student production of the musical crammed into a tiny college hall.
explanation.walkthrough: POLY is short for polytechnic, a kind of British college; 'put on in' puts K and I inside it. 'The', 'and' and 'but' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a small, poky, confined way.

clue.text: Sea states required for a jellyfish?

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
USA, the United States of America

explanation.surface: A question about which seas and states one needs to find a jellyfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required for a' is a link; the question mark admits the definition is a stage of the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The free-swimming bell-shaped form of a cnidarian is the familiar jellyfish stage.

clue.text: Avoiding contact in an informal gathering

parts.note: the article an gives the letter A
a social is a casual party or get-together

explanation.surface: Someone keeping to themselves at a friendly get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shunning the company of other people.

clue.text: Bill twice taking first-class return? That is a bloomer!

indicators.note: taking means having the next part added on
repeated two times, so the abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: the first-class symbol is turned back to front

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: Two invoices for a first-class return trip, which is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' is not a mistake but a flowering plant. A1 is written AI; 'return' reverses it to IA. 'That is a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The wattle tree flowers in bright yellow sprays, so it is a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Royal seat, formerly, in the High Court

definitions.meaning: a division of the English High Court, long so named under male sovereigns

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a monarch's place to sit, and also a historic division of the English High Court.

clue.text: Elissa, otherwise, achieved nothing

parts.note: did means achieved, as in 'did it'
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone otherwise known as Elissa accomplished nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Elissa is the other name of the Queen of Carthage in Virgil.
explanation.definitionFit: The founding queen of Carthage was also known as Elissa in classical sources.

clue.text: Currency bringing Latin air of excitement

indicators.note: excited letters are agitated and stirred up

explanation.surface: Money bringing a thrilling Latin air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of excitement' rearranges AIR; 'bringing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The former money of Italy and present money of Turkey.

clue.text: Authority showing impropriety

explanation.surface: A permit that reveals wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means formal permission and also abuse of freedom, as in poetic or wanton excess.

clue.text: Greek character opposed to Italian wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against

explanation.surface: A Greek fellow who will not drink Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from the Tuscan region of Italy.

clue.text: How well do we receive Anne Bronte with a pseudonym?

definitions.text: How well do we receive Anne Bronte with a pseudonym?

parts.words: How well do we receive Anne Bronte with a pseudonym?
parts.note: Anne Bronte wrote as Acton Bell, so her initial is plainly A. Bell, and a perfectly clear signal is received in the same words

explanation.surface: A question about how readers take to the novelist writing under a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Bronte published as Acton Bell: Anne's (A's) clear as A. Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a signal or sound received with perfect clarity.
